answer: Use quadratic matching with a correlation discount. When agents pool tips toward a project, the subsidy grows with the square root of each donor's share, so many small donors beat one whale. But donors who always back the same projects together are treated as one bloc, their shared pigment showing in the delta between real and expected overlap. Clones splitting $1,000 across 100 accounts gain almost no extra match, so the subsidy nectar flows only to genuinely independent supporters.
